'''''Ornithopus sativus''''', the '''serradella''', '''pink serradella''' or '''common birdsfoot''', is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Fabaceae]].<ref name="23086-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:510872-1 |title=''Ornithopus'' L. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=28 July 2021 }}</ref><ref name="NSW-DPIRD">{{cite web|url=https://www.dpird.nsw.gov.au/agriculture/pastures-and-rangelands/species-varieties/serradella/part-a|title=Serradella - Part A Introduction|author=<!--Not stated-->|website=NSW Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development |publisher=NSW Government |access-date=5 September 2026 }}</ref> It is native to Southwestern Europe and Northwest Africa in Portugal, western Spain, northern Morocco and Algeria, and southwestern France and has been introduced as a legume [[forage]] to many locations around the world, including most of central and eastern Europe, Turkey, the Caucasus, the Azores, South Africa, Kenya, [[Java]], most of Australia, the [[North Island]] of New Zealand, southern Chile, and California.<ref name="510872-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:510872-1 |title=''Ornithopus sativus'' Brot. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=28 July 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ornithopus sativus |url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/07_49%20Ornithopus.pdf |publisher=[[Flora Iberica]] |access-date=28 May 2022}}</ref> It is known for producing a high{{nbh}}quality forage in highly acidic, nutrient{{nbh}}poor soils.<ref name="1_of_2230_Google_Scholar_Hits" >{{cite journal |title=The breeding system of ''Ornithopus sativus'' Brot. subsp. ''sativus'' |year=2021 |last1=Nutt |first1=Bradley J. |last2=Harrison |first2=Robert J. |last3=McComb |first3=Jen A. |last4=Howieson |first4=John G. |journal=Grass and Forage Science |volume=76 |issue=1 |pages=3–9 |doi=10.1111/gfs.12521 |bibcode=2021GForS..76....3N }}</ref> Its name derives from the birdsfoot-shaped cluster of pods.<ref name="NSW-DPIRD" />
